stress.notes: Acordo Ortográfico 1990 conventions: paroxytone default; written accents override; final -i/-u/-r/-l/-z/-x/-im/-om/-um/-ins/-ons/-uns and nasal diphthongs attract final stress. Unmarked -em/-ens/-am stay paroxytone (homem, homens, falam): an oxytone of more than one syllable in -em or -ens is written with an acute (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base VIII, 1.º c: deténs, haréns, provéns, também). DIPHTHONGS: declared so the bundled syllabifier counts nuclei correctly. Without them every vowel run merges into one nucleus, so co-e-lho is read as coe-lho — one syllable short — and the stress, and therefore the unstressed-vowel reduction it conditions, land on the wrong vowel. ⟨oe⟩ is hiatus, not a diphthong, and is absent from this list for that reason (Cunha & Cintra, Nova Gramática do Português Contemporâneo, §Ditongos). COMPOUNDS: a hyphenated compound is one prosodic word. Each element keeps its own stress and the last is the strongest (Bechara, Moderna Gramática Portuguesa, p. 340, quoted in Ciberdúvidas, resposta 28042), so compound_stress is "last": Infopédia gives guarda-chuva [ɡwardɐˈʃuvɐ], with the primary stress on chuva. IPA_DIPHTHONGS is empty: the grapheme table writes every diphthong with a glide ([aj], [uj], [ɐ̃w̃]), so two full vowels side by side in the transcription are always a hiatus, and the stress mark is placed with each IPA vowel as a nucleus of its own. Read with the orthographic list, the IPA [ui] of ⟨proíbe⟩ /pɾuibɨ/ and [iu] of ⟨viúva⟩ merge into one syllable and the mark lands a syllable early. The acute on a tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a vowel marks exactly this hiatus (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 1.º: juízes, ruína, ciúme, miúdo, saída, baú). CLOSED HIATUS: a tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a vowel takes no acute when it forms a syllable with the next consonant, and it is still a nucleus in hiatus: "As vogais tónicas/tônicas grafadas i e u das palavras oxítonas e paroxítonas não levam acento agudo quando, antecedidas de vogal com que não formam ditongo, constituem sílaba com a consoante seguinte, como é o caso de nh, l, m, n, r e z: bainha, moinho, rainha; adail, paul, Raul; Aboim, Coimbra, ruim; ainda, constituinte, oriundo, ruins, triunfo; atrair, demiurgo, influir, influirmos; juiz, raiz, etc." (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 2.º, Portal da Língua Portuguesa, acordo.php?action=acordo&version=1990). closed_hiatus states it: the ⟨i u⟩ of ⟨ai au ei eu iu oi ui⟩ is split off before ⟨nh⟩, or before l m n r z when no vowel follows and the letter does not start ⟨lh rr⟩. ⟨ou⟩ is left out: Base X, 2.º gives no ⟨ou⟩ example, and the ⟨ou⟩ words of this shape are loans and foreign names (Lourdes, gourmet, tour). A following ⟨s⟩ is excluded (Base X, 1.º: "excetuando o caso de s"), so animais keeps its diphthong. The split holds only where the ⟨i u⟩ is stressed: Base XIV, 1.º says the spelling does not tell an atonic ⟨i u⟩ in hiatus from a diphthong (arruinar, faiscar), so an atonic one keeps the diphthong reading. FINAL DIPHTHONGS: a final ⟨iu ui⟩ after a vowel is one stressed diphthong, and the vowel before it is a nucleus of its own: "Prescinde-se do acento agudo nos ditongos tónicos/tônicos grafados iu e ui, quando precedidos de vogal: distraiu, instruiu, pauis (pl. de paul)." (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 6.º, Portal da Língua Portuguesa, acordo.php?action=acordo&version=1990). So distraiu is dis-tra-iu and pauis is pa-uis, not dis-trai-u and pau-is. final_diphthongs states it for a word-final ⟨iu ui⟩, alone or before ⟨s⟩. A medial ⟨iu ui⟩ after a vowel is outside it: Base X, 4.º reads a tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a diphthong there (baiuca, cauila). A final one cannot have that reading unwritten, because Base X, 5.º writes the acute on a final tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a diphthong (Piauí, teiú, teiús). The split holds only where the diphthong is stressed. Cruz-Ferreira (1999: 128) lists [iu] (viu) and [ui] (anuis [ɐˈnuiʃ]) among the falling diphthongs, and transcribes desistiu /dɨziʃˈtiu/ with the stress on the diphthong (p. 129). The vowel before the diphthong is pretonic and reduces, as before the hiatus of the infinitive: sair [sɐˈir], distrair [diʃtrɐˈir], instruir [ĩʃtruˈir], paul [pɐˈuɫ] (Infopédia). TONIC AFTER DIPHTHONG: a stressed ⟨i u⟩ after a diphthong is a syllable of its own, and the diphthong keeps its glide: "Prescinde-se do acento agudo nas vogais tónicas/tônicas grafadas i e u das palavras paroxítonas, quando elas estão precedidas de ditongo: baiuca, boiuno, cauila (var. cauira), cheiinho (de cheio), saiinha (de saia)." (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 4.º) and "Levam, porém, acento agudo as vogais tónicas/tônicas grafadas i e u quando, precedidas de ditongo, pertencem a palavras oxítonas e estão em posição final ou seguidas de s: Piauí, teiú, teiús, tuiuiú, tuiuiús. Obs.: Se, neste caso, a consoante final for diferente de s, tais vogais dispensam o acento agudo: cauim." (Base X, 5.º, Portal da Língua Portuguesa, acordo.php?action=acordo&version=1990). So baiuca is bai-u-ca and teiú is tei-ú. tonic_after_diphthong states it: where the stressed written syllable starts with ⟨i u í ú⟩ after a syllable that ends in a listed diphthong, the glide stays in the syllable before and the mark follows it. The rule reads only the place of the mark: the transcription already writes the glide and the vowel. An unstressed ⟨i u⟩ after a diphthong is outside it. Infopédia divides these words so and writes the mark after the glide: bai.u.ca [bɐjˈukɐ], boi.u.no [bojˈunu], mai.ús.cu.la [majˈuʃkulɐ], tei.ú [tɐjˈu], fei.u.ra [fɐjˈurɐ]. It divides tui.ui.ú and cau.im the same way, but its readings [tujuˈju] and [kɐˈwĩ] have the mark before the glide. The unstressed ⟨i u⟩ keeps its place: a.bai.u.ca.do [ɐbajuˈkadu], a.bai.u.car [ɐbajuˈkar]. NASAL DIPHTHONG ⟨ãi⟩: "Os ditongos representados por vogal com til e semivogal são quatro, considerando-se apenas a língua padrão contemporânea: ãe (usado em vocábulos oxítonos e derivados), ãi (usado em vocábulos anoxítonos e derivados), ão e õe. Exemplos: cães, Guimarães, mãe, mãezinha; cãibas, cãibeiro, cãibra, zãibo; [...]" (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base VII, 3 a), Portal da Língua Portuguesa, acordo.php?action=acordo&version=1990). So ⟨ãi⟩ is one nucleus, the diphthong of ⟨ãe⟩, and the grapheme table gives it the reading of ⟨ãe⟩. It is not in final_stress_endings, because Base VII, 3 a) uses it in anoxytones: cãibra is cãi-bra, stressed on the diphthong. Cruz-Ferreira (1999: 128) lists the nasal diphthong [ɐ̃i] (cem [sɐ̃i]), and Infopédia gives cãibra [ˈkɐ̃j̃brɐ] and zãibo [ˈzɐ̃j̃bu] with the nucleus of mãe [ˈmɐ̃j̃].
